parsed_response.concise_technical_rationale: Node V-001 and associated lines; deviation is low pressure in the crude input line and separator V-001 (CASE-01, CASE-02). The source ranks it frequency B, severity I, Low risk, with no existing safeguard listed (CASE-03). The proposed action is the source's own recommendation: confirm the PIT-101 low-pressure alarm is active in the control room and activate it only if the check shows a need. It is a detection/indication measure, not a newly installed layer. Read numerically, 95 of 100 demands succeed: 95% success, equivalently 5% unavailability. That means about 95 indicated and about 5 unindicated demands over the next 100 eligible demands. The gain wording does not change this, and facts and cost are frame-invariant (CASE-04). With no listed safeguard today, an alarm delivering control-room indication on about 95% of demands gives operators a meaningful early warning for a fixed 20-unit cost. The Low risk ranking reduces urgency but does not argue against a modest, source-recommended check-and-activate action. Limits: the 95% covers indication only, not operator response, accident prevention or elimination of residual risk. Cost-effectiveness cannot be quantified because budget scale, demand rate and consequence cost are unspecified. Recommendation: approve. Document the check, verify the setpoint and annunciation, and include the alarm in routine testing and alarm management so the 5% unavailability is managed rather than assumed to be zero.
